🇨🇭 Swiss quantum hardware attracts serious seed capital

@ZuriQ, a spin-off from @ETH Zurich, has raised USD 25.5 million in a seed round led by @Quantonation to advance its trapped-ion quantum computing architecture.

Why it matters:
⚛️ A seed round of this size signals that quantum hardware in Europe is moving from lab curiosity to fundable engineering, with investors underwriting multi-year technical roadmaps rather than short product cycles.
🇨🇭 Switzerland's advantage is compounding: decades of ion trap and photonics research, deep talent pipelines out of ETH and EPFL, and founders who build capital-efficiently because they were trained in environments where precision matters more than speed.
🔭 Specialised quantum hardware is the foundation layer for the next decade of computation, from materials discovery to cryptography. Whoever controls the hardware stack controls the economics on top of it.

We keep seeing the same pattern in Swiss DeepTech: hard science, disciplined spending, global ambition from day one.

https://zuriq.com/

🇨🇭 Rivers as infrastructure, data and urban destiny

Researchers at @EPFL have published work on how rivers shape the growth of cities and the structure of societies, per @EPFL News.

Why it matters:
🌊 Water systems are becoming a measurable input for infrastructure planning, insurance modelling and climate risk pricing, a market that is expanding as cities face flooding and drought in the same decade.
🇨🇭 Switzerland sits at the hydrological heart of Europe and has built world-class expertise in hydrology, remote sensing and environmental modelling, a combination few countries can match at this density.
🏙️ The broader implication: urban planning is shifting from intuition to simulation. That opens space for Swiss spin-offs commercialising environmental data, digital twins and predictive modelling tools for governments and industry.

Academic research like this is often the quiet origin of the DeepTech companies we back five years later.

https://actu.epfl.ch/news/how-rivers-shape-cities-and-societies

🇨🇭 Open AI infrastructure gets a Swiss upgrade

@Apertus has released Apertus 1.5, the next iteration of its open AI infrastructure, developed within the Swiss research ecosystem alongside @EPFL and @ETH Zurich.

Why it matters:
🧠 Open models with transparent training data address the compliance gap that keeps regulated industries, banks, hospitals, public administrations, from deploying frontier AI at scale.
🇨🇭 Switzerland can offer something scarce: sovereign compute, neutrality, strict data protection and public research capacity, all in one jurisdiction. That is a genuine commercial differentiator, not a slogan.
🏗️ Open infrastructure lowers the entry cost for the next layer of applications. Startups building on top of it spend less on foundation models and more on solving actual customer problems, which is exactly how capital-efficient DeepTech compounds.

The interesting question now is how many Swiss companies build on this base over the next 18 months.

http://apertus-ai.org

🇨🇭 Industrial cost intelligence becomes a software category

@Valuemize has closed a seven-figure pre-seed round to scale its software for product cost management in manufacturing and industrial engineering.

Why it matters:
📉 Cost engineering remains a spreadsheet discipline in much of European manufacturing. Digitising it touches procurement, design and margin decisions simultaneously, which makes the entry point narrow and the expansion path wide.
🇨🇭 Swiss industry gives local software founders something rare: demanding reference customers in precision manufacturing, machinery and medtech who will pay for accuracy and tolerate no guesswork.
⚙️ Beyond cost savings, this is about decision speed. Engineering teams that price design choices in real time ship better products faster, and that advantage accumulates across every product generation.

A reminder that not all DeepTech is hardware. Software built on deep domain knowledge can be just as defensible, and considerably more capital-efficient.

https://www.valuemize.io/en

🇨🇭 Swiss gene editing advances toward in vivo delivery

@Immitra Bio has raised CHF 2.4 million to develop its in vivo gene editing platform, according to @Venturelab Swiss.

Why it matters:
🧬 In vivo editing is the field's central bottleneck: the editing tools work, delivering them safely to the right cells does not, yet. Capital is now concentrating on exactly that problem.
🇨🇭 Switzerland's life sciences density (research institutes, contract manufacturers, regulatory expertise and pharma headquarters within a two-hour radius) lets small teams run serious biology on modest budgets.
💊 If delivery is solved, the addressable set of genetic diseases expands dramatically, and the treatment model shifts from chronic management toward single-administration therapy.

Early-stage biotech in Switzerland tends to be lean by necessity. That discipline often produces sharper milestones and better data per franc spent, which is precisely the profile we look for.

https://www.venturelab.swiss/Immitra-Bio-raises-CHF-24-million-to-advance-invivo-gene-editing-platform

🇨🇭 Neutral compute layers become strategic ground

@SkyPilot, founded by a @Databricks cofounder, has raised USD 20 million to build a vendor-neutral orchestration layer for AI compute, positioning itself as the neutral ground between cloud providers.

Why it matters:
☁️ Compute has become the largest line item for AI-native companies. Software that arbitrages across providers turns infrastructure from a fixed cost into a variable one, which changes unit economics materially.
🇨🇭 The neutrality framing is telling: Swiss positioning is being used as shorthand for trust and independence in the AI stack. Local companies should treat that reputation as an asset to monetise, not just to admire.
🔀 Portability weakens vendor lock-in and makes serious AI work viable for teams without hyperscaler-sized budgets. For European DeepTech, that is a direct route to doing more with less capital.

The orchestration layer rarely gets attention, yet it quietly determines who can afford to compete.

https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/ai-orchestration-market-107177

🇨🇭 Neighbours start studying the Swiss DeepTech model

Austria's @WKO has published an analysis of Swiss DeepTech success and the opportunities it creates for Austrian companies, per @wko.at.

Why it matters:
📈 When foreign trade bodies write playbooks about your ecosystem, the signal is clear: Swiss DeepTech has moved from promising to benchmark, and cross-border partnerships will follow the attention.
🇨🇭 The underlying formula is not mysterious: two world-class federal institutes, dense industrial demand, strong IP protection and a funding culture that rewards technical milestones over growth theatre.
🤝 Regional integration is the next step. Swiss scale-ups need European customers, talent and follow-on capital, while neighbouring industry needs access to frontier technology. Both sides gain.

The challenge remains the same one we work on daily: making sure Swiss companies scale from Switzerland rather than relocating the moment growth capital arrives.

https://www.wko.at/aussenwirtschaft/schweiz-deep-tech-erfolg
